title: FACS Sorting of Live Cells for 10x scRNASeq
author: Maigan Brusko
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfqzjmx6
materials: a. Prepare 1X LD Green (Invitrogen) as directed by the manufacturer. b. Resuspend at 1x10 6 /mL in 1X LD Green and incubate at RT for 20 minutes. c. Add 3mL Stain Buffer. d. Pellet cells at 350g for 5 min. Decant supernatant e. Resuspend the cells at 10-15x10 6 /mL in cold PBS with 2% FBS f. Hold the tubes in an ice bucket with a cover to protect the cells from light.

steps.title: Thaw cells and warm media
steps.instruction: Warm 10 mL of cDMEM at 37 °C in a 15 mL conical tube (bead bath). Thaw each cryovial of cells in a 37 °C water bath, add 1 mL cDMEM to the cryovial, then transfer the cells to the 10 mL of room‑temperature cDMEM. Because cDMEM is used twice, aliquot a total of 20 mL cDMEM per cryovial (10 mL for thawing, 10 mL for later resuspension).

steps.title: Centrifuge and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 10 min. Decant the supernatant, using a 1000 µL pipette to remove any remaining liquid. Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of room‑temperature cDMEM. Pipette 20 µL into a small Eppendorf tube for cell counting. After counting, centrifuge again at 300 × g for 7 min.

steps.title: Prepare FACS collection tubes
steps.instruction: Label two FACS tubes. Coat the inside of each tube with 0.5 mL FBS and vortex briefly. Add 500 µL PBS containing 10 % FBS to each tube and keep the tubes on ice until sorting.

steps.title: Prepare and verify fluid system
steps.instruction: Check sheath and waste tank levels and fill or empty as needed. Ensure fluid and air lines are disconnected from the ethanol tank and connected to the sheath tank. Verify that the closed‑loop nozzle is installed in the flow cell. Prepare fresh 20 % Contrad solution, 20 % bleach solution, and sterile filtered DI water for later cleaning steps.

steps.title: Start cytometer and warm lasers
steps.instruction: Start the computer and launch FACSDiva. Power on the cytometer by pressing the main power button. Wait 30 minutes for the lasers to warm up. In the Cytometer window, double‑check fluidics levels and replenish or empty waste as required.

steps.title: Fluidics startup and initial cleaning
steps.instruction: In FACSDiva select Fluidics Startup. Verify that air and fluid lines are disconnected from the ethanol tank and connected to the sheath tank, then click Done. Verify that a closed‑loop nozzle is installed, then click Done and allow the startup to complete. When prompted, click Done and OK on subsequent dialogs. Clean the flow cell: select Cytometer → Cleaning Modes → Clean Flow Cell, install a tube with ~5 mL 20 % Contrad and click OK; repeat this step two more times. Repeat the three‑cycle cleaning with 20 % bleach, then repeat with sterile filtered DI water (at least three total cycles).

steps.title: Swap to 70 µm nozzle
steps.instruction: Open the cytometer hood. Turn the nozzle‑locking lever counter‑clockwise to the 6:00 position and remove the closed‑loop nozzle. Insert the 70‑µm nozzle (ensure O‑ring present and the word TOP faces up). Lock the nozzle by turning the black key to the right. Verify that the setup mode matches the 70‑µm nozzle via Sort → Sort Setup.

steps.title: Configure stream and breakoff
steps.instruction: If the Breakoff and Side Stream windows are not visible, click the Sorting button in the Workspace toolbar. Click the Stream button in the Breakoff window to turn the stream on. Open the sort block door and confirm the stream flows smoothly into the waste aspirator. Adjust the Ampl slider until the drop breakoff appears in the top third of the Breakoff window (do not exceed 70 V). Verify that satellite droplets merge with the large droplets. Enter the measured Drop 1 value in the Drop 1 field. Turn on the Sweet Spot to maintain a stable drop pattern.

steps.title: CST performance check
steps.instruction: Turn off the Sweet Spot (if on) and select Cytometer → CST. The interface switches to CS&T. Verify that the bead lot under Setup Beads matches the CS&T bead lot; select the correct ID if needed. Retrieve CST beads from the fridge and gently invert the vial to mix. In a 12 × 75‑mm tube add 0.35 mL sheath fluid and one drop of beads, then install the bead tube on the loading port. In the Setup Control window choose Check Performance → Run and wait ~5 minutes. Confirm a green checkmark and “Passed” status. Close the CS&T window (File → Exit) and click Use CST Settings to update laser delay, area scaling, etc. Turn the Sweet Spot back on for the next step.

steps.title: Determine drop delay with Accudrop beads
steps.instruction: Open the Accudrop Drop Delay experiment template (or create a new experiment). Expand Specimen_001 → Tube_001 and set the current tube pointer to Tube_001. Open the sort layout by double‑clicking it. Load a tube containing approximately one to two drops of Accudrop beads in 2 mL sheath fluid. Adjust the flow rate to achieve 1,000–3,000 events / s; if this cannot be reached with a flow rate between 1 and 5, adjust bead concentration. Turn on the voltage in the Side Stream window, click Sort, then Cancel (beads are sent to waste). Adjust the micrometer dial for the brightest bead spot on the center stream. Click the Optical Filter button, then the Auto Delay button, and start the run. Monitor progress until an announcement confirms the drop delay is set. Optimize the delay: set sort precision to Fine Tune, adjust the delay arrow until the left side‑stream intensity is ≥98 % (target ~100 %). Click Optical Filter again to move the emission filter away, then turn off the voltage (deflection plates). Unload the Accudrop beads and load DI water for future experiments; keep the Sweet Spot on and the stream stable.

steps.title: Test sort and set collection tubes
steps.instruction: Install the two collection tubes in the collection‑tube holder, attach the holder to the cytometer, slide it into the slotted fittings below the sort aspirator drawer, and close the sort collection chamber door. Verify that the water bath for the holder is on and at the set temperature. In the Side Stream window click the Voltage button to turn on the deflection plates; confirm the stream image does not move. Click the Test Sort button. Because this is a one‑way sort, set all voltage sliders to zero except the one that corresponds to the intended collection tube (e.g., left stream). Open the aspirator drawer (Waste Drawer button), open the sort block door, and aim the active side stream into the collection tube while adjusting its slider. Close the sort lock door. Do not touch the charged plates (12 kV potential).

steps.title: Create experiment, gating, and event targets
steps.instruction: Verify that the cytometer configuration matches the 70‑µm nozzle. Create a new experiment folder, add one specimen, and create the desired number of tubes; label folders, specimen, and tubes as needed. In the worksheet window, create plots and gates: (i) forward‑ and side‑scatter to exclude debris and doublets; (ii) amine‑reactive viability dye (FITC channel, excitation max ≈ 495 nm) to select live cells. Define the number of events to record per tube (typically 10,000 if possible). Replace the test‑sort collection tube with the FBS‑coated FACS tube prepared in Step 3.

steps.title: Configure sort layout
steps.instruction: Click the New Sort Layout button on the Browser toolbar. Change the device menu to 4 tubes (only one will be used). Set the sort precision mode to 4‑Way Purity. Choose a target number of events (specific number or Continuous). Select a Save Sort Reports option (None, All, or Ask User). Add the required cell population to the left‑column sort location (right‑click the location and choose the population); leave all other locations empty.

steps.title: Load sample and perform sorting
steps.instruction: Verify that the collection tubes are installed in the positions matching the sort layout and voltage sliders. Install the sample tube onto the loading port and click Load. Adjust the flow rate (lower rates improve sorting; do not exceed 7,000 events / s). If the flow rate is set to 1 and events exceed 7,000 / s, add PBS with 2 % FBS to the sample to reduce cell concentration. Verify that the current tube pointer indicates the correct tube, then click Sort. Confirm any prompts to open the aspirator drawer or turn on the deflection plates. Click Record Data to save data for the tube; acquisition and sorting continue until the specified number of events is reached. Monitor sort progress in the Sort Layout window (events sorted, sort rate, conflict rate, efficiency). Stop acquisition before the sample tube runs dry.

steps.title: Stop acquisition and wash cells
steps.instruction: When the sample tube is close to empty, click Stop Acquiring in the Acquisition Dashboard. Transfer the collection tubes to an ice bucket. Wash the cell suspensions three times in PBS containing 0.04 % BSA before proceeding to the 10x Genomics protocol.

steps.title: Clean tubing and fluid pathway
steps.instruction: Ensure the stream is on. Load approximately 10 mL of 20 % bleach and run for 10–15 minutes at flow rate 10. Unload the bleach tube. Load approximately 10 mL of DI water and run for 10–15 minutes at flow rate 10. Unload the DI water and turn off the stream.

steps.title: Clean flow cell
steps.instruction: Open the cytometer hood. Turn the nozzle‑locking lever counter‑clockwise to the 6:00 position and remove the nozzle. Replace it with the metal closed‑loop nozzle (waste line attached, O‑ring present, TOP up). Turn the black key to the right to lock the nozzle. Select Cytometer → Cleaning Modes → Clean Flow Cell. Install a tube with ~3 mL sterile filtered DI water and click OK. Repeat the DI water cleaning step at least two more times.

steps.title: Perform fluidic shutdown
steps.instruction: Make sure the stream is off and unload any sample tube. Check the ethanol shutdown tank and refill if needed. Select Cytometer → Fluidics Shutdown. Remove the nozzle from the flow‑cell assembly and click Done. Insert the integrated closed‑loop nozzle (verify O‑ring) and click Done. Connect the fluid line from the sheath filter to the ethanol filter on the shutdown tank (keep the sheath filter attached to the sheath tank). Connect the air line from the sheath tank to the air port on the ethanol shutdown tank. Click Done to start the cleaning process. When prompted, install a tube containing 3 mL sterile filtered DI water on the loading port and click Done. After the process completes, click OK. Vent air pressure from the sheath tank by pulling up on the ring of the pressure‑relief valve. Turn off the cytometer main power, exit FACSDiva, and shut down the computer.
